critical_acquisition_defect_found_and_re.cause: core.autocrlf was true in the inherited Windows Git configuration (global was empty, so it came from the system config), and the MONN repository ships no .gitattributes marking its pickles as binary
critical_acquisition_defect_found_and_re.effect: every one of the six source files failed its SHA-256 check on first clone, each LARGER than the manifest size
critical_acquisition_defect_found_and_re.repair: git config core.autocrlf false; git config core.eol lf; git rm --cached -r .; git reset --hard <pinned commit>
critical_acquisition_defect_found_and_re.post_repair: all six byte counts and SHA-256 values match the manifest exactly
critical_acquisition_defect_found_and_re.significance: without the supplied manifest hashes this corruption would have been silent and would have produced a subtly wrong corpus. Any future acquisition of this source on Windows MUST disable autocrlf before checkout.
critical_acquisition_defect_found_and_re.generalisation: this is a property of the acquisition environment, not of MONN; it would affect any binary-bearing repository cloned under the same configuration

affinity_label_firewall.mechanism: rebuild_monn_edge_corpus.py reads only the two interaction pickles; the TSV paths appear nowhere in its execution path. This audit hashed the TSVs as byte streams without parsing them.
affinity_label_firewall.independently_checked: the script source was read in full before execution; it loads only EXPECTED[split]['path'], which are the two interaction dictionaries
